newsitem.title: RUSSIA: "Crime and Punishment" axeman stalks Russian city.
newsitem.headline: "Crime and Punishment" axeman stalks Russian city.

text.p: The Russian city of Izhevsk, home of the Kalashnikov automatic rifle, is living in fear of a more primitive killer -- an axe-murderer police compare to the hero of Fyodor Dostoyevsky's classic novel "Crime and Punishment".
The man has axed to death three elderly women, all living alone, after gaining entry to their homes posing as a plumber.

"You might say we have our own Raskolnikov," Izhevsk police spokesman Sergei Klimok told Reuters on Thursday, referring to the student who slays an old woman money-lender with an axe in Dostoyevsky's 1866 study of sin and remorse in tsarist Russia.
A fourth woman survived an attack, providing a description of a man in his 20s which has been distributed around the city along with police warnings to be wary of strangers at the door.
Over the past 50 years, Izhevsk, 800 km (500 miles) east of Moscow, has produced millions of AK47s and other types of Kalashnikov, making it the world's most popular firearm.
